subject: ACME MSA & Order Form — availability and support redlines
messages:
From: Contracts (Acme) <contracts@acme.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-04-18T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: MSA & Order Form redlines — SLA / maintenance windows

Karthik,

Thanks for the packet earlier. Please find attached our redlines to the MSA and Order Form focusing on availability and support obligations. High-level asks from Acme Ops/legal:  

- Uptime target of 99.95% (monthly) for the services we will run in production.
- Escalation / response times: Sev1 within 1 hour, Sev2 within 2 hours (we flagged the latter as critical).
- Service credit formula that scales more aggressively (we proposed 5%, 15%, 30% bands) with no hard cap tied to monthly fees.
- Maintenance windows limited to two 4-hour windows per month with explicit blackout periods for our peak times (Thu 12:00–18:00 ET). Planned maintenance to be approved at least 7 business days in advance.
- Requirement for a post-incident RCA within 72 hours for Sev1 incidents.

Can we set up a 30 min call to go through these items? We’d like to align before routing to our procurement team. Attached: ACME_MSA_redlines_v1.pdf

Best,
Maya R. (Contracts)
Acme Corp — Legal & Contracts
contracts@acme.com

--
Attachment: ACME_MSA_redlines_v1.pdf (annotated PDF, 12 pages)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Contracts (Acme) <contracts@acme.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-04-18T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form redlines — SLA / maintenance windows

Hi Maya — thanks, received the redlines and the annotated Order Form. Helpful to see Acme’s priorities laid out. Quick responses and where we think compromise might land: 

- Uptime (99.95%): that level is achievable for Dedicated / reserved capacity customers with the appropriate capacity reservations and monitoring. For standard Hosted customers (shared pools) our baseline offering is 99.9%. We can offer a Premium Availability add-on that delivers 99.95% (we'd include a pricing delta).

- Response times: Sev1 (P1) — agree on 1 hour. Sev2/P2 — our usual is 4 hours for Hosted; with Dedicated or 24x7 support add-on we can commit to 2 hours.

- Service credits: we prefer a capped, predictable schedule to avoid unlimited exposure (industry standard). Proposed table: 
  * <99.9% = 5% credit
  * 99.9%–99.95% = 15% credit
  * <99.8% = 30% credit (capped at 100% of monthly service fees).
This is negotiable — we can expand caps for Enterprise deals with a higher commitment.

- Maintenance windows: propose two 6-hour windows per month (to allow staged rollouts and runway) but with a firm prohibition on changes during Acme blackout periods unless mutually agreed. We will commit to 7 business days notice for planned maintenance.

- RCA timing: we can commit to initial incident summaries within 24 hours and a full RCA within 72 hours for Sev1.

Attached: Redline_SLA_proposal_karthik_v2.pdf with track changes to the Order Form clauses and a suggested credit table.

Suggested next step: 30-min sync on Wednesday 2029-04-20 at 10:00 AM PT to walk through the delta and confirm whether Acme wants Dedicated capacity or the Premium Availability add-on. If that works I’ll also loop in Solutions and Finance to scope pricing.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

--
Attachment: Redline_SLA_proposal_karthik_v2.pdf (word doc, 6 pages)
From: Ops (Acme) <ops@acme.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Contracts (Acme) <contracts@acme.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-04-19T13:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form redlines — SLA / maintenance windows

On Thu, Apr 18, 2029 at 11:05 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com> wrote:
> - Uptime (99.95%): that level is achievable for Dedicated / reserved capacity customers...
> - Response times: Sev1 (P1) — agree on 1 hour. Sev2/P2 — our usual is 4 hours for Hosted; with Dedicated or 24x7 support add-on we can commit to 2 hours.

Thanks for the quick reply. A couple of clarifications and push-backs from our side: 

- Acme requires the 99.95% SLA across the board for platform availability — we can’t accept patchwork availability differentiated by plan for our production workloads. If Redwood needs to gate that behind Dedicated pricing, we need transparency on the capacity reservation required (GPU counts / throughput metrics) and guaranteed procurement timelines.

- Service credit scaling: we appreciate the proposed table but cannot accept a hard cap at 100% of monthly fees for severe multi-day outages. We propose a scale that continues to accumulate for successive missed months (e.g., 15% for month 1, 30% for month 2, and escalating).

- Maintenance windows: our peak periods are Thu 12:00–18:00 ET. We will not accept maintenance that impacts those windows. We also want a maximum of two 4-hour planned maintenance windows per calendar month. Emergency maintenance is understood, but must be communicated and compensated per the credit schedule.

- RCA: 72 hours is acceptable for a full RCA, but we require an initial incident timeline within 4 hours and regular updates until resolution.

Attaching our annotated Order Form (ACME_OrderForm_annotated_ops.pdf). We are prepared to escalate to procurement once we have clarity on the availability model and the credit accumulation mechanism.

Regards,
Sandeep Rao
Head of Infrastructure Operations, Acme
ops@acme.com

--
Attachment: ACME_OrderForm_annotated_ops.pdf (3 pages)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Contracts (Acme) <contracts@acme.com>, Ops (Acme) <ops@acme.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-04-20T15:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form redlines — SLA / maintenance windows

Thanks Sandeep / Maya — good, constructive feedback. I summarized our proposed compromise and next steps below to get everyone aligned before legal/ procurement routing.

Summary of proposed compromise:
- Availability: Offer an "Enterprise Availability" add-on that guarantees 99.95% across Acme production workloads. This will be delivered via dedicated capacity reservations (detailed sizing to be provided by Solutions). We will include a Service Level Exhibit in the Order Form that references the add-on.
- Credits: Replace the single-month cap with a tiered accumulation approach for successive missed months (15% month 1, 30% month 2, escalation clause thereafter) with a negotiated maximum liability tied to the term length.
- Response times: Commit to Sev1 initial acknowledgement within 1 hour and continuous updates; for Sev2 we will commit to 2 hours with the Enterprise Availability add-on (4 hours for standard Hosted).
- Maintenance: Firmly prohibit planned Maintenance during Acme blackout windows. Commit to at most two planned windows per calendar month, each up to 4 hours, unless a different cadence is agreed. 7 business days notice for planned maintenance; emergency maintenance per incident policy.
- RCA: Initial incident timeline / summary within 4 hours, full RCA within 72 hours for Sev1.

Action items / mutual action plan:
1) Solutions (Kimberly) will produce a sizing & pricing worksheet for the Enterprise Availability add-on by 2029-04-22.
2) Legal (Lauren) to review the proposed Service Level Exhibit language and the revised credit accumulation language; aim for sign-off or concrete redlines by 2029-04-24.
3) Karthik to host a 30-min technical + commercial call with Acme on 2029-04-22 at 10:00 AM PT (invite to follow).
4) Move agreed-upon Order Form to DocuSign once legal redlines are resolved.

If this plan looks acceptable I’ll have Kim drop the sizing worksheet into the shared Drive and Lauren will circulate the legal redline draft. Happy to join the procurement call once you have dates.

Thanks all — appreciate the rapid back-and-forth.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198
